slides.title: Switch Statement
slides.content: A switch statement tests a single variable against multiple possible values using case labels.

slides.title: Case and Break
slides.content: Each case labels a value. break exits the switch so execution does not fall through to the next case.

slides.title: Default Case
slides.content: The default case handles any value that does not match an explicit case.

slides.title: Multiple Cases
slides.content: You can stack multiple case labels before one block to execute the same code for different values.

exercise.prompt: Print 'Vowel' for both case 'a' and case 'e'
exercise.starterCode:
char letter = 'a';
// Write your switch below
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: switch
When run, your code should output: Vowel

slides.title: Switch Expressions
slides.content: Switch expressions return a value directly using =>. They replace verbose switch statements for simple mappings.

exercise.prompt: The discard pattern in switch expressions uses _____

slides.title: Pattern Matching
slides.content: Switch expressions support type patterns, letting you branch based on type or property values.

exercise.prompt: What does _ represent in a switch expression?

slides.title: When Clauses
slides.content: Use when to add extra conditions to a case or switch arm beyond simple equality.

slides.title: Switch Best Practices
slides.content: Prefer switch expressions for value mappings. Always include a default or discard case to handle unexpected input.
